title: Starter Eval Harness
description: A minimal eval harness: load test cases from a JSON file, run each input through the agent, check the property functions, and write a timestamped results file.

steps.description: This is the starter harness for Exercise 2. The page says it loads test cases from a JSON file, runs each through the agent, checks the defined property functions, and writes a timestamped results file.
The comment shows the `test_cases.json` format: a list of objects, each with an `id`, an `input`, and an `expected_properties` list naming the properties to check.
`open("test_cases.json")` reads the file, and `json.load` turns it into the list `cases`.

The loop runs each case. `run_agent(case["input"])` produces the output, and the comment marks that line as your agent call. For each property name in the case, it calls `PROPERTY_FUNCTIONS[prop_name]` on the output and records the result under that case's `id`.
The last lines save a timestamped file. `datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")` builds the timestamp, and the results are written to `eval_results_<timestamp>.json` as indented JSON.

steps.question: The page says the timestamped results file is what lets you compare two runs how, later?
